newsitem.title: DUBAI: U.S. warns of possible further attacks in Saudi.
newsitem.headline: U.S. warns of possible further attacks in Saudi.

text.p: The United States embassy in Saudi Arabia has warned it continues to receive unconfirmed reports of possible attacks on U.S. interests in the kingdom and urged Americans to exercise extreme caution.

The warning, issued on an embassy emergency telephone line and dated January 25, was addressed to the 35,000 Americans living in Saudi Arabia, where two bomb blasts killed 24 Americans in the past 14 months.
It updated a similar alert on December 21.

The embassy said it "continues to receive new information suggesting that terrorist actions against U.S. interests in Saudi Arabia remain possible. These reports, while unconfirmed, are reason for concern and reinforce the need for continued vigilance and alertness."

It said in the past several months the embassy and U.S. military forces in the kingdom "have reviewed their security posture and made improvements wherever possible to lessen their vulnerability" especially for the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan which ends in the second week of February.

"The U.S. government strongly encourages all American residents of the kingdom to likewise take appropriate steps to increase their security awareness and lessen their vulnerability," it said, adding that Americans should exercise "extreme caution in matters concerning security".
It said Saudi officials continued to work closely with the embassy to ensure the safety of Americans in the kingdom.
Security has been tightened at complexes housing Americans in Saudi Arabia following the November 1995 and June 1996 bombings and continued reports of possible further attacks.

About 4,000 of the 5,700 U.S. troops in the kingdom, part of coalition forces enforcing a "no-fly zone" over southern Iraq, have relocated to a remote air base southeast of Riyadh, where strict security measures have been implemented.
The first bombing, at a U.S.-run military training centre in Riyadh, killed seven people -- five Americans and two Indians. Four Saudi nationals were beheaded for the attack.
Another bomb killed 19 American servicemen when a fuel truck blew up at a complex housing U.S. military personnel in the eastern city of Khobar on June 25.
